questions.q: Where was Dr. Livesey when Jim and Mr. Dance arrived at his house?
choices: At the hall, dining with the squire
Visiting a sick patient in Bristol
Asleep upstairs in his bedroom
At the Admiral Benbow with Jim's mother
questions.evidence: gone up to the hall to dine and pass the evening with the squire

questions.q: What did the squire's black, quick-moving eyebrows suggest about him?
choices: A quick and high temper
A gentle and shy nature
Great wisdom and learning
A deep and lasting sadness
questions.evidence: this gave him a look of some temper, not bad, you would say, but quick and high

choices: Mr. Trelawney
Mr. Dance
Mr. Dogger
Mr. Redruth
questions.evidence: Mr. Trelawney (that, you will remember, was the squire's name)

questions.q: How did the squire react when he heard how Jim's mother went back to the inn?
choices: He cried "Bravo!" and broke his pipe on the grate
He scolded her for being so foolish and reckless with her life
He yawned and fell asleep by the fire
He sent a servant off to fetch the constable
questions.evidence: the squire cried "Bravo!" and broke his long pipe against the grate

questions.q: What did the doctor do right after Jim handed him the oilskin packet?
choices: Put it in his coat pocket without opening it
Tore it open at once and spread it on the table
Threw it straight into the fire to burn it
Handed it over to Mr. Dance to keep
questions.evidence: he put it quietly in the pocket of his coat

questions.q: How did the squire describe Flint?
choices: The bloodthirstiest buccaneer that sailed
A kind sailor who had been wrongly accused
A Spanish admiral who fought the English
A poor fisherman from the Bristol docks
questions.evidence: He was the bloodthirstiest buccaneer that sailed.

questions.q: The doctor calls the squire "hot-headed and exclamatory." What does "exclamatory" mean?
choices: Always crying out loudly
Very calm, quiet and patient
Good at solving hard puzzles
Easily tired out by any work
questions.evidence: you are so confoundedly hot-headed and exclamatory

questions.q: What two things were inside the oilskin packet?
choices: A book and a sealed paper
A rolled map and a brass key
A pistol and a letter
Gold coins and a compass
questions.evidence: It contained two things--a book and a sealed paper.

questions.q: According to the squire, what did the crosses in the captain's book stand for?
choices: Ships or towns the pirates sank or robbed
Men the captain had buried on lonely islands
Days the captain had spent away at sea
Bottles of rum the captain had drunk
questions.evidence: These crosses stand for the names of ships or towns that they sank or plundered.

questions.q: Why did the amounts in the account-book grow larger over time?
choices: The captain rose in rank among the pirates
Prices went up a great deal every single year
He stopped spending any of his money
He added interest to his savings
questions.evidence: the amounts increase, you see, as he rose in rank

questions.q: What was the island on the map said to be shaped like?
choices: A fat dragon standing up
A thin crescent moon
A sleeping cat curled in a ball
A horseshoe
questions.evidence: shaped, you might say, like a fat dragon standing up

questions.q: What was written beside the red cross in the southwest of the island?
choices: "Bulk of treasure here."
"Bones, his pile."
"No more rum."
"The arms are here."

questions.q: What job did the squire say Jim would have on the voyage?
choices: Cabin-boy
Ship's cook
Ship's doctor
Lookout

questions.q: Whom did Dr. Livesey say he was afraid of, and why?
choices: The squire, because he could not hold his tongue
Pew, because the blind man might come back for revenge
Mr. Dance, because he might try to steal the map
Jim, because he was too young to keep a secret
questions.evidence: "You," replied the doctor; "for you cannot hold your tongue.
